question: How much will Gold Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q3 2026? (Sep 7 - Sep 18)

calls.reasoning: Base rate first: over 2000-2026 gold and S&P futures price returns have near-identical long-run CAGRs (~8.2% vs ~8.7% price-only), so the median 2-week gold-minus-S&P spread is ~0pp with all the action in dispersion, not drift. I stay essentially at that anchor: the window's dominant event (FOMC Sep 16, hike odds quoted 50-66% across the last week, plus a dot plot) is a genuine coin flip whose surprise is already priced both ways, and Aug CPI lands Sep 11. Directional adjustments cancel - hawkish Warsh Fed and the Sep 4 pattern (hot payrolls: gold -2.4% vs S&P -0.38%) are gold-negative, while the live Strait of Hormuz/Iran premium, a 34-50% dovish-hold surprise to which gold has the larger beta, weak late-September equity seasonality, and S&P futures excluding dividends tilt the other way; net median +0.2pp. Dispersion is the real answer: gold's 2026 realized vol is roughly 1.6x the S&P's, giving ~4.8pp of two-week spread sd. Both bounds are open and 2026 has repeatedly delivered >10pp two-week divergences (a -9% single gold day on Jan 30, a -28% Q2 slide, a +9.6% August), so I price real escape mass on both sides: a hawkish 50bp/hot-dots shock resuming the correction while equities hold on strong growth (down), or Hormuz escalation or a Fed-independence shock spiking gold into an equity selloff (up). Evidence on gold's September seasonality was directly contradictory across sources, so I gave it no weight. No prediction market matches this contract, so nothing to blend against.

Dispersion is the real content: CPI (Sep 11) and FOMC+dots (Sep 16) both land inside a 9-session window, and gold's rate beta is ~5-6x the S&P's, so the spread inherits gold's vol almost undiluted.
